o1.biggest_strength: Immaculate Doist brand voice, crisp copy, and strict discipline around the one-tip, one-button rule.
o1.biggest_mistake: Email 5 is essentially a re-try of Email 2 sent only to non-adopters, leaving successful users stranded without a fifth touchpoint.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give successful users an appropriate fifth email instead of duplicating the recurring-task concept, or graduate them gracefully into a delayed Pro or workflow email.

o2.biggest_strength: Brilliant strategic decision to move Pro to Day 14 gated exclusively to activated users, giving the business a complete activation-to-monetization journey without annoying free users.
o2.biggest_mistake: The copy is slightly less minimalist than Output 1, though still well within brand guidelines.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Trim one or two explanatory sentences in the body copy to match Output 1's punchy conciseness.

reason: Both nailed the core retention metrics, platform branching, and tone. Output 2 wins because keeping Pro at Day 14 gated strictly to active users is smarter business than Output 1's plan to send a duplicate repeating-task email as Email 5.
